title: Prefetch Governor and Pathway Selection for Safe Cost Tuning
creator: Maya Alvarez
description: Add a coordinated prefetch governor and pathway selection layer that recommends batching/caching configuration changes, applies them with staged canaries, and enforces latency/throughput SLO guardrails via limiters and SLO-aware routing. This ticket implements the runtime and control-plane pieces needed to safely apply aggressive cost-saving suggestions (e.g., longer cache TTLs, prefix prefetch heuristics, larger batch windows) while guaranteeing customer-facing SLOs and automated rollback on anomalies.
background: We have multiple separate initiatives producing batching/caching recommendations (OptimizeAdvisor, Autosuggest Batching Profiles) but applying changes has risk: regressions in tail latency or throughput due to workload shifts. Current processes rely on manual reviews + coarse canaries. We need an orchestrated governor that 1) converts recommendations into safe config deltas, 2) enforces runtime limiters and per-pathway routing to protect SLOs, and 3) automates detection and rollback for anomalies observed during rollout.
proposed_solution:
1) Prefetch Governor: a control-plane component that translates advisor recommendations into parameterized profiles (prefetch window size, prefix cache TTL, batch aggregation thresholds) and a safety envelope (min/max bounds, backoff behavior). 2) Pathway Selection: tag serving routes by latency-sensitivity and throughput elasticity and select candidate pathways for cost tuning (e.g., background embeddings vs. interactive chat). 3) SLO-aware Routing: add a routing policy that routes a percentage of traffic to tuned pathway variants based on realtime SLO headroom (latency P95/P99 and QPS headroom). 4) Runtime Limiters: implement lightweight per-worker budget and circuit breakers that throttle tuned variants when per-shard tail latency or token throughput degradation is detected. 5) Anomaly Detector: statistical detector (EWMA + seasonality-aware CUSUM) that monitors regressions relative to baseline and triggers automated rollback and alerts. 6) Safe Apply Engine: staged rollout (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated health gates and optional manual hold.

Implementation notes: keep change small in runtime (feature flags) and implement governor as an independent microservice integrated with rollout orchestration and console Dashboard for visibility.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Feature flag gated dev deployment + unit/integration tests. Phase 1 (Canary): enable governor for non-production traffic with synthetic load tests. Phase 2 (Blue-Green Canary): 1% of production traffic for 60m. If no SLO alerts, progress to 5% for 2h, then 20% for 4h, then 50% for 24h, then 100%. During each step: run canary verifications (latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, token throughput, KV cache hit ratio) and ensure anomaly detector score < threshold. All steps revert automatically if a health gate fails.

Escalation: on auto-rollback, paging to on-call runtime eng + PM, open incident with prefilled template.
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: 1) P95 or P99 latency increase > 15% sustained for 3 consecutive windows (5m windows) or 2) error rate increase > 0.5% absolute or 200% relative (whichever smaller) or 3) throughput degradation causing customer-facing quota violations. Rollback options: immediate automatic rollback to previous profile, progressive throttle of tuned pathway, or manual rollback. Rollback action must be idempotent and preserve metrics tags so postmortem comparisons are accurate.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert if p99 increases > 15% sustained for 15m
Alert if kv_cache_hit_ratio drops > 10% and coincides with latency increase
SLO burn rate alert at 0.5x for tuned_variants
acceptance_criteria: Governor accepts advisor recommendations and emits bounded config deltas
Staged rollout works with automated gates and can progress to 100% in staging
Anomaly detector triggers rollback on synthetic regression (automated test)
Per-pathway routing respects SLO headroom and does not route tuned variants when headroom < 10%
Dashboards show tuned_variant tag and associated metrics
